title: CacheBlend: Fast Large Language Model Serving for RAG with Cached Knowledge Fusion

components.name: KVCacheStore
components.purpose: Maps each input text chunk (identified by hash) to its pre-computed per-layer KV cache, persisted on a single storage device (CPU RAM or NVMe SSD), with LRU eviction when full. Enables retrieval of pre-computed KV for any reused chunk during inference and async write-back for new chunks.

inputs.name: text_chunk
inputs.description: A text chunk produced by Langchain chunking; key for the hash table.

outputs.name: kv_cache_layer
outputs.shape_or_type: Tuple[K, V] where K, V have shape (num_kv_heads, chunk_len, head_dim)
outputs.description: Per-layer K and V tensors for the chunk; returned as -1 / sentinel if absent.

algorithm_source.paper_section: Section 5.1 (KV cache store) and Section 6 (Managing KV cache)

hyperparameters.storage_levels: single level: CPU RAM or NVMe SSD
hyperparameters.hash_function: vllm.utils.hashing.sha256_cbor over (parent_hash, token_id_block) [RESOLVED via official_code, LMCache lmcache/v1/token_database.py]
hyperparameters.kv_dtype_on_disk: model native activation dtype (fp16 / bf16); no quantization [RESOLVED via official_code, vllm_blend xformers.py:229]
hyperparameters.on_disk_file_layout: per (chunk_hash, layer_id) shard; CacheEngineKey = model@world@worker@chunk_hash@dtype@layer_id [RESOLVED via official_code, LMCache lmcache/utils.py:373]

unknowns: [LOW-CONF] Exact size threshold that triggers LRU eviction (capacity not specified in paper or code; assume sized to fit eval working set ~25 GB on 1 TB NVMe so eviction is effectively off during measurement).

components.name: PositionalEncodingRecovery
components.purpose: Recovers RoPE positional encodings when a pre-computed KV cache (originally encoded at a different absolute position) is concatenated into a new context at a new absolute position. The recovery exploits the fact that RoPE attention only depends on relative position.

inputs.name: K_pre
inputs.description: Pre-computed K vectors for a chunk, stored in pre-rotation form (rotation applied lazily at new positions).

inputs.name: original_position
inputs.description: Absolute position m at which K was originally encoded (effectively 0 since K is stored without rotation in the official impl).

inputs.name: new_position
inputs.description: Absolute position m' at which the chunk is placed in the concatenated input.

outputs.name: K_pre_repositioned
outputs.description: K vectors with RoPE applied at the new absolute positions so that attention scores depend only on relative distance.

hyperparameters.implementation: explicit forward RoPE rotation of loaded K with new absolute positions; calls self.rotary_emb(new_positions, fake_q, K_pre); per-layer, on-the-fly inside LlamaAttention.forward [RESOLVED via official_code, vllm_blend llama.py:174-179]
hyperparameters.non_rope_models: out of scope; deferred to future work (Mamba, Griffin) [RESOLVED via paper, Section 9]

components.name: SelectiveKVRecompute
components.purpose: On each transformer layer, recompute Q, K, V only for the currently selected HKVD tokens, while reusing the loaded pre-computed K/V for the remaining tokens. Produces the layer's output embeddings used as input to the next layer.

inputs.name: input_tensor
inputs.description: Hidden state input to the current transformer layer for the full concatenated context.

inputs.name: input_metadata
inputs.description: Original vLLM layer metadata needed for prefill (positions, attn metadata, etc.).

inputs.name: HKVD_indices
inputs.description: Indices of the selected HKVD tokens whose KV will be recomputed at this layer.

inputs.name: check_flag
inputs.description: If True, this layer will (re)select HKVD tokens based on deviation between newly computed and loaded KV. If False, only the existing HKVD_indices are recomputed.

inputs.name: KVCache_pre_layer
inputs.shape_or_type: Tuple[K_pre, V_pre] of shape (num_kv_heads, seq_len, head_dim)
inputs.description: Loaded pre-computed KV for this layer (after positional recovery).

outputs.name: output_tensor
outputs.description: Layer output, used as input to the next layer.

outputs.name: KVCache_new_layer
outputs.shape_or_type: Tuple[K_new, V_new] of shape (num_kv_heads, seq_len, head_dim)
outputs.description: Per-layer KV cache where selected tokens have freshly recomputed K/V and others retain pre-computed K/V.

outputs.name: HKVD_indices_next
outputs.description: Indices propagated to the next layer; if check_flag was True, may be updated to top-r% by KV deviation.

algorithm_source.paper_section: Section 4.2 (Selectively recomputing KV cache); Section 6 (prefill_layer interface)

hyperparameters.compute_overhead_proportionality: r% of full prefill compute per layer
hyperparameters.softmax_denominator_scope: all keys / standard 1/sqrt(d_k) scaling; selected Q attends to full-length expanded K,V [RESOLVED via official_code, vllm_blend xformers.py:240-441]
hyperparameters.mask_expansion_strategy: positional recovery applied per-layer on-the-fly before expansion [RESOLVED via official_code, vllm_blend llama.py:174-179]
hyperparameters.partial_kv_writeback: in-place fancy-indexed assignment along seq dim (key_old[imp_indices] = key; value_old[imp_indices] = value), equivalent to index_copy_ [RESOLVED via official_code, vllm_blend xformers.py:240-245]

components.name: HKVDSelector
components.purpose: Identify the subset of tokens whose KV must be recomputed per layer (High-KV-Deviation, HKVD). Released implementation selects once at a single 'check layer' and reuses for all subsequent layers, instead of the gradual-decay schedule described qualitatively in the paper.

inputs.name: V_new_layer_i
inputs.description: Newly computed V for the candidate set at the check layer.

inputs.name: V_pre_layer_i
inputs.description: Pre-computed (loaded) V for the candidate set at the check layer (after positional recovery).

inputs.name: r_percent
inputs.description: Target recompute ratio (single scalar in the released code, e.g. 0.15, 0.16, or 0.18).

outputs.name: HKVD_indices
outputs.description: Indices of top-r% tokens by per-token squared-L2 V-deviation; reused on all subsequent layers.

algorithm_source.paper_section: Section 4.3 (Selecting which tokens to recompute, Insight 1 and Insight 2, gradual-filtering scheme)
equation_numbers: Delta_kv(KV_i, KV_full_i)[j] = sum over (head, head_dim) of (V_new[j] - V_pre[j])^2
Selection rule: top-r% by V deviation

hyperparameters.first_layer_candidate_set: all tokens in the concatenated context
hyperparameters.schedule: single check layer at decoder index 1; HKVD selected there is reused on all later layers [RESOLVED via official_code, vllm_blend llama.py:300 (check_layers:[1]) and 350-356]
hyperparameters.deviation_reduction: per-token squared L2 norm of (V_new - V_pre), summed across head and head_dim axes [RESOLVED via official_code, vllm_blend xformers.py:210-211]
hyperparameters.deviation_tensor: V only (not K, not concatenated [K;V]) [RESOLVED via official_code, vllm_blend xformers.py:210]
hyperparameters.check_flag_per_layer: True only on layer index 1; False on all other layers (status 0/1/2 encoding) [RESOLVED via official_code, vllm_blend llama.py:350-356]

components.name: Fusor
components.purpose: Drive layer-by-layer selective recompute for a single request: for each layer, wait for that layer's pre-computed KV to finish loading from storage, run prefill_layer with the current HKVD set, then update HKVD_indices for the next layer; conceptually runs in parallel with KV loading thread.

inputs.name: concatenated_text_chunks
inputs.description: Ordered list of retrieved chunks (top-6) plus user query.

inputs.name: recompute_ratio_r
inputs.description: Target average recompute ratio chosen by LoadingController.

outputs.name: fused_kv_cache
outputs.shape_or_type: List[(K_l, V_l)] of length num_layers, each (num_kv_heads, total_len, head_dim)
outputs.description: Final fused KV cache ready for decoding.

algorithm_source.paper_section: Section 5.1 (Fusor); Section 5.2 (Putting them together); Section 6 (Integrating Fusor)

hyperparameters.fetch_kv_miss_behavior: fall back to full prefill (status=0 path) for the affected chunk; the released code triggers this implicitly via cache_fuse_metadata['check']=False [RESOLVED via official_code, vllm_blend llama.py:330-356]

unknowns: [LOW-CONF] Exact synchronization primitive used by synchronize() (CUDA event vs threading.Event vs torch.cuda.Stream): the released CacheBlend prototype is not actually pipelined. ASSUMPTION: dedicated torch.cuda.Stream for host->device KV copy, default stream for prefill, torch.cuda.Event for layer hand-off, threading.Thread for host fetch loop.
[LOW-CONF] Whether prefill_layer pipelines compute on a non-default CUDA stream: same ASSUMPTION as above.

components.name: LoadingController
components.purpose: Pick the recompute ratio r and the storage device so that loading delay covers (>=) recompute delay per layer, while enforcing r >= r* (quality floor). Also chooses the cheapest storage device among those that satisfy this constraint.

inputs.name: L
inputs.description: Total context length in tokens for the current request.

inputs.name: storage_devices
inputs.description: Available devices with measured Throughput(device) and per-byte storage cost.

outputs.name: device
outputs.description: Chosen storage device (CPU RAM or NVMe SSD).

equation_numbers: T_recompute(r%, LLM, L) = r% * Prefill(LLM, L)
T_load(LLM, L, storage_device) = PerTokenKVSize(LLM) * L / Throughput(storage_device)

hyperparameters.selection_rule_step1: r% such that T_recompute(r%) == T_load(device); then r = max(r%, r*)
hyperparameters.selection_rule_step2: Among devices with T_recompute(15%) >= T_load(device), pick cheapest by C_store
hyperparameters.PerTokenKVSize_formula: 2 * num_layers * num_kv_heads * head_dim * sizeof(activation_dtype); e.g., Mistral-7B fp16 = 131072 B/token; Yi-34B fp16 = 245760 B/token; Llama-70B fp16 = 327680 B/token [RESOLVED via paper + standard]

unknowns: [LOW-CONF] Closed-form C_store(LLM, L, T, storage_device): paper introduces it abstractly. ASSUMPTION: C_store = bytes * time * price_per_byte_per_time(device); collapses to latency-only for the paper's single-NVMe+CPU-RAM setup.
[LOW-CONF] How Prefill(LLM, L) is profiled (granularity, batch size). ASSUMPTION: batch_size=1, sweep L in {512,1024,2048,4096,8192}, fit a*L + b*L^2.

pipeline: 1. User submits a query. Retriever (SentenceTransformers + L2 distance over a Langchain-chunked DB) returns top-6 chunks of 512 tokens.

2. KVCacheStore is queried via fetch_kv(chunk_text, layer_id) for each retrieved chunk. Hashes are computed (vLLM sha256_cbor block hashing); present chunks are scheduled to load from CPU/SSD, missing chunks are flagged for full recompute and async write-back.
3. LoadingController computes r% via T_recompute / T_load equations and picks device; selects r = max(estimated r, r* = 15%).
4. PositionalEncodingRecovery rewrites RoPE per-layer for each loaded chunk's K (rotary_emb called with new absolute positions and a dummy fake_q).

5. Fusor runs layer-by-layer: thread A calls synchronize() then prefill_layer(input_dict, KVCache_i); thread B prefetches KVCache_{i+1} via fetch_kv concurrently. NOTE: the released prototype runs sequentially; two-thread pipelining is the conceptual design.

6. Inside prefill_layer at the single check layer (decoder index 1): the layer is first prefilled on the full candidate set, V deviation (sum over head and head_dim of (V_new - V_pre)^2) is measured, and top-r% indices update HKVD_indices reused for all subsequent layers. For layers != 1, only KV for current HKVD_indices is recomputed (status=2). Non-selected tokens keep pre-computed K/V (key_old[imp_indices] = key; value_old[imp_indices] = value).
7. After all layers complete, the fused KV cache is handed to the vLLM decoding engine which generates the answer auto-regressively.
8. Any newly computed KV (for new or missing chunks) is moved to CPU via torch.cpu() and written back to disk asynchronously via torch.save().
